Subject: IO pricing / model roster for a pilot

Hi Rafael,

Quick intro — I run product at Clarity Health. We're evaluating hosted vendors for a 3-month pilot: summarization + QA over clinical notes (~3M tokens/mo expected, spiky bursts) with a potential expansion to 50M tokens/mo if pilot looks good.

Can you send your standard per-1M token pricing split by input / output for the hosted API and a short list of recommended (verified) models for summarization and question-answering (latency/cost tradeoffs)? A few other items that procurement will need:
- Any volume discount tiers (e.g., 12-month commit pricing) and example thresholds
- Whether streaming responses are charged at the same output rate
- SOC2 status and whether SSO / SAML is available on hosted
- Any POC credits / pilot pricing you offer (we're often offered a small credit to run realistic workloads)

If possible, please attach your latest rate card and a condensed model roster we can share with engineering. Happy to hop on a short call this week if that's easier.

Thanks,

Hi Sofia — great to meet you (virtually). Thanks for the clear ask — putting the short answers below and attaching the rate card + model roster. Ben (cc) will help with a formal quote and Lauren can jump in on contract/procurement questions.

Short answers:
- Standard hosted IO rates (per 1M tokens):
  * Gen-Base (low-latency family, e.g., RW-7B): Input $350 / 1M tokens, Output $760 / 1M tokens
  * Gen-Prod (higher quality, e.g., RW-13B / 70B optimized): Input $980 / 1M tokens, Output $2,050 / 1M tokens
  * Distilled QL (cost-optimized for high-throughput summarization): Input $120 / 1M tokens, Output $240 / 1M tokens
  Note: rates above are list; committed/volume pricing available (see below).

- Streaming: streaming output is charged on the same output-per-token basis. We count tokens on the canonical byte-pair encoding used by the model; for chat-style usage both prompt (input) and generated tokens (output) are billed separately.

- Volume discounts / commits: typical tiers we offer (example):
  * Monthly usage < 10M tokens: list rates
  * 10M–50M tokens: 10% off list
  * 50M–200M tokens: 20% off list
  * 200M+ or 12-month committed contracts: custom pricing (we've done 25–40% for multi-year, high-commit deals)
  For your 3M pilot we typically propose a short-term PO + option to convert to a committed tier if you hit thresholds.

- Pilot credits: we can provide an onboarding credit equal to 5M tokens (applied as credit to your account) for a 3-month pilot. If you convert to a 12-month commit within 30 days of pilot close, we apply an additional one-time onboarding credit.

- Compliance / SSO: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II certified (summary enclosed). Hosted customers have SAML SSO and optional enterprise settings for session control; private deployments available if you require VPC or air-gapped options.

Attached: redwood_ratecard_1m_v2.pdf, hosted_model_catalog_202703.pdf.

If useful, I can draft a simple quote (PO-ready) that maps your expected pilot volume and the optional 12-month commitment scenarios — Ben, could you prepare that and include an example invoice / payment term (Net 30) and a sample SLA?

Regards,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Carlos — looping in the draft quote and the sample invoice you requested. Answers inline:

1) Token counting: we bill for all tokens submitted to the model (system + user + metadata) as "input" tokens; output is the tokens generated by the model. For chat-style usage we provide tooling that estimates the monthly bill given your templates; we can run an import of a representative prompt set to estimate billing impact.

2) Streaming billing: we bill generated tokens as they are produced; if the client abandons a stream early we only bill for tokens actually generated and delivered. Retransmits triggered by client-side retries are not billed if they include identical byte ranges and the retry flag is set — in standard HTTP streaming flows this is rare.

3) Pilot credit: the 5M token pilot credit is an account-level credit applied to invoices until exhausted; it will appear as a credit line on the invoice (not a line-item discount).

Attached: clarity_draft_quote_CLAR-2027-01.pdf (PO-ready), sample_invoice_clar_3M_distilled.pdf (example math). Payment terms: Net 30 standard; we can support Net 60 for enterprise procurement on a case-by-case basis.

Next steps: Rafael / Sofia — if you'd like, I'll schedule a 30-min call to walk through the invoice math and the model choices. Rafael, can you confirm availability tomorrow morning?

Thanks,
